name: Mahat
title: Levite and Temple Servant
summary: Mahat was a Levite of the Kohathite clan who served during King Hezekiah's religious reforms in Judah. He was one of the appointed overseers over the gifts, tithes, and holy offerings in the house of the Lord. Mahat is also mentioned in the genealogies of the Levites who served in the temple.

keyEvents.title: Levitical Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Mahat is mentioned as the son of Amasai in the genealogy of the Levitical temple singers of the Kohathite clan.

keyEvents.title: Hezekiah's Temple Reform
keyEvents.description: During King Hezekiah's religious reforms, Mahat was among the Levites called to cleanse and reopen the temple.

keyEvents.title: Overseer of Temple Offerings
keyEvents.description: Mahat was appointed as one of the overseers under the Levite Konaniah to manage the gifts, tithes, and holy offerings brought to the house of the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Hezekiah's Restoration of Worship
keyEvents.description: As part of Hezekiah's extensive reforms, the Levites, including Mahat, were assigned to ensure the fair distribution of temple income to the priests and Levites.

keyEvents.title: The Faithful Service of the Levites
keyEvents.description: Mahat served faithfully in his role as a Levite and helped restore right worship of the Lord after a period of spiritual decline under earlier kings.
